strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses real memory constraints in ultra-high-resolution optical flow estimation with clear problem articulation and hardware limitations
Insightful empirical analysis: compelling evidence that only 1.6% of correlation volume cells are sampled, motivating the sparse computation approach
Clever optimization design: patch-major layout reformatting improves sparsity by 58% without computational overhead—an elegant engineering contribution

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: isolated benchmarks with baselines, end-to-end evaluation across multiple datasets (8K, Sintel, KITTI, Spring), multiple hardware platforms, and thorough ablation studies
Strong practical results: up to 58% end-to-end RAFT speedup, 95% memory reduction, and enables 8K optical flow on consumer hardware
Valuable benchmark resource: 8K CHARGE dataset with super-resolved ground truth fills gap in high-resolution optical flow evaluation
Clear presentation and reproducibility: well-structured paper with effective visualizations, algorithm pseudocode, and extensive supplementary material
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: core contribution (block-sparse matrix multiplication with patch-major layout) applies established techniques to the correlation volume problem. The key insight (1.6% sampling) could motivate alternative approaches not explored

Significant overhead at lower resolutions limits universality: Table 1 shows 36.1% runtime overhead at 1024px input; method provides no speedup at low resolutions where default implementation already works well

Caching mechanism complexity contradicts claims: growth factor of 2 with 5GB buffer appears heuristic-driven. 'Non-negligible memory overhead' undermines the low-memory claim, and no sensitivity analysis on caching parameters provided

Incomplete on-demand baseline analysis: on-demand sampling underperforms by up to 90%, but paper only mentions 'not hardware-friendly' without profiling, kernel analysis, or investigation of alternative implementations

Cascaded inference contribution is orthogonal: Section 6.2's multi-scale warm-start is independent of correlation sampling and could apply to any method, diluting focus and conflating two research directions
Limited dataset diversity: 8K benchmark uses single Blender movie (3 shots, 335 frames) with forward-flow-only evaluation, narrowing conclusions about real-world high-resolution content
Block size selection under-explored: B=8 fixed throughout with B=16 heuristic for high-res. No principled selection strategy or analysis of interaction with image content and motion patterns
Vague implementation details: proxy cost volume construction (Section 4.4) unclear; CUDA kernel specifics not provided; no code availability statement mentioned
Performance degradation at extreme scales: Table 6 shows 79.2% improvement at 8192px (vs 91.9% at 2048px). Degradation with resolution not analyzed or discussed
Incomplete failure case analysis: no discussion of when method is not beneficial, how sparsity degrades with fast motion/occlusions, or pathological access patterns
